title: Sandstone and Saucer: A Trail-Running Week in the Karkonosze and Góry Stołowe
subRegion: The Sudetes — Karkonosze, Góry Stołowe and the Śnieżnik Massif

bestPeriod.window: the first three weeks of September — dry sandstone, stable air, empty ridge
bestPeriod.avoid: late July–August (Karpacz and Karłów at full crowd), and November–April when the paved ridge trails ice over

transport.note: €90–€160 (Wrocław transfer, one rental-car day, buses, Kopa chairlift)

activities.note: €35–€60 (two national park tickets, Szczeliniec, Błędne Skały, Jaskinia Niedźwiedzia)

gatewayAirport: Wrocław (WRO), 2 h by bus/car to Karpacz; Prague (PRG) 2 h 30 to Kudowa via Náchod. Rail to Jelenia Góra, then bus 100/200 to Karpacz (~40 min).
summary: Two ranges, ninety kilometres apart, that run nothing alike. The Karkonosze give you a bald granite ridge on the Czech border, peat bog on duckboards, glacial cirques dropping away on your left, and stone-paved paths…
hook: Two ranges, ninety kilometres apart, that run nothing alike. The Karkonosze give you a bald granite ridge on the Czech border, peat bog on duckboards, glacial cirques dropping away on your left, and stone-paved paths that turn into a skating rink the moment it rains. The Góry Stołowe give you a sandstone tabletop split into labyrinths you run through sideways. Come for the contrast, and bring shoes with a hard edge.

snapshot.Start / End: Karpacz → Kudowa-Zdrój (two bases, one relocation on Day 4)
snapshot.Getting there: Wrocław (WRO), 2 h by bus/car to Karpacz; Prague (PRG) 2 h 30 to Kudowa via Náchod. Rail to Jelenia Góra, then bus 100/200 to Karpacz (~40 min).

itinerary.title: Arrival and the Łomniczka warm-up
itinerary.morning: Fly into Wrocław, bus or drive to **Karpacz**. Buy the Karkonoski Park Narodowy ticket online at kpnmab.pl or at the gate — around 15 PLN (€3.50) a day, reduced roughly half [VERIFY: 2026 KPN daily entry tariff].
itinerary.afternoon: Ease in on the green trail up **Kocioł Łomniczki** from Karpacz Górny, following the Łomniczka stream past the waterfall to the cirque headwall. Turn at the Dom Śląski junction and descend the same way. It is steep, rooted and rocky — a calibration run for what the rest of the week costs your ankles.
itinerary.evening: Eat at Karczma Głodny Turysta on Konstytucji 3 Maja and walk the town's odd Norwegian stave church, **Świątynia Wang**, moved here from Vang in 1842 [VERIFY: current Wang opening hours].

itinerary.title: Śnieżka the honest way
itinerary.morning: Leave Karpacz Biały Jar by 07:00 on the blue trail through the Kocioł Łomniczki, then the zigzags to **Dom Śląski** at 1,400 m. Fill bottles here. The final cone to **Śnieżka (1,603 m)** is 25 minutes of stone stair.
itinerary.afternoon: On the summit: the three fibreglass discs of the **Wysokogórskie Obserwatorium Meteorologiczne** (1974, and it does look like a stack of flying saucers), the baroque **Kaplica św. Wawrzyńca** of 1681, and the Czech **Poštovna** hut serving soup. The border runs over the top; you cross it by walking.
itinerary.evening: Descend the red ridge west then the trail past **Strzecha Akademicka** and **Samotnia** at Mały Staw — the most photographed hut in Poland, on a tarn under a 200 m cirque wall — and down to Karpacz. Beer at Samotnia is worth the ten-minute stop.

itinerary.title: The full Droga Przyjaźni
itinerary.morning: First bus to **Szklarska Poręba**, chairlift or the black trail up to **Szrenica (1,362 m)**, then east on the red-blazed **Droga Przyjaźni Polsko-Czeskiej**. Łabski Szczyt, then the rim of the **Śnieżne Kotły** — two glacial cirques with 250 m walls and the mock-castle transmitter building on the lip.
itinerary.afternoon: Wielki Szyszak, Przełęcz Karkonoska (water at **Odrodzenie**), then the long boardwalk across **Równia pod Śnieżką**, a high peat bog at 1,400 m. This is the fastest running of the week and the coldest place to be caught in weather.
itinerary.evening: Second summit of Śnieżka if the sky allows, then the Kopa chairlift or the blue trail down to Karpacz. Pierogi ruskie and żurek at Bączek in Karpacz.

itinerary.title: Wielki Staw, then relocate
itinerary.morning: A short, beautiful loop: the trail from Karpacz to **Wielki Staw**, the larger of the two Karkonosze tarns, sitting in a cirque directly beneath the ridge, and back over Kopa. Run it before 09:00 and you will have the water to yourself.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive or take the bus via Jelenia Góra and Kłodzko to **Kudowa-Zdrój** (2 h 15 by car, longer by public transport). Book a car for Days 4–7 if you can — the Stołowe trailheads are poorly linked.
itinerary.evening: Walk the spa park in Kudowa, drink the mineral water from the pijalnia, and eat at Restauracja Sowia Dolina [VERIFY: current opening hours].

itinerary.title: The sandstone labyrinth
itinerary.morning: Drive to **Karłów** and take the 665 stone steps up **Szczeliniec Wielki (919 m)**, the flat-topped sandstone block that is the signature of the range. Entry is ticketed separately from the park [VERIFY: 2026 Szczeliniec entry price]. Inside: **Piekiełko** ("Little Hell"), the slot corridors, the ladders, and the Fotel Pradziada viewpoint over the whole Kłodzko basin.
itinerary.afternoon: It is a one-way circuit with fixed direction and you cannot run it — accept that. Descend to Karłów and run the yellow trail to **Schronisko Pasterka** and the Skały Puchacza viewpoint instead, which is properly runnable sandstone singletrack.
itinerary.evening: Back to Kudowa. If you want a genuinely odd hour, the Kaplica Czaszek at Czermna is a chapel lined with several thousand human skulls [VERIFY: current chapel opening hours].

itinerary.title: Błędne Skały and the Skalne Grzyby
itinerary.morning: Drive the toll road up to **Błędne Skały** (853 m) at opening. It is a maze of sandstone blocks with passages — Tunel, Kuchnia, the Ucho Igielne — narrow enough that a broad-shouldered runner with a vest on genuinely wedges. Take the pack off first. One-way, timed entry in summer.
itinerary.afternoon: Run the red then blue trails east across the plateau to the **Skalne Grzyby**, the "rock mushrooms" — free-standing sandstone toadstools scattered through the forest between Batorów and Karłów. This is the best running in the Stołowe: rolling, sandy, quiet, no ticket gate.
itinerary.evening: Return via Karłów. Eat at Bar Karłów by the car park; simple and open when everything else is not.

itinerary.title: Śnieżnik and a bear cave
itinerary.morning: Drive to **Kletno** (1 h 20 from Kudowa) and book the first slot at **Jaskinia Niedźwiedzia**, the Bear Cave — timed entry, limited daily numbers, and it fills [VERIFY: 2026 Jaskinia Niedźwiedzia ticket price and booking window].
itinerary.afternoon: Run the trail from Kletno up to **Schronisko na Śnieżniku** and on to the summit of **Śnieżnik (1,425 m)**, a bald grass dome on the Polish–Czech border with the new Czech observation tower on the far side. Open, fast, exposed — this is a run, not a scramble.
itinerary.evening: Descend the same way and drive out to Wrocław (2 h 30) or back to Kudowa for a last night.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Vivaldi
accommodationStrategy.description: on Olimpijska, ten minutes' jog from the Biały Jar trailhead and the Kopa chairlift base, with a pool and sauna that do real work on trashed calves after the ridge day.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–8 weeks ahead direct or via Booking; avoid Polish long weekends, when Karpacz doubles in price.

accommodationStrategy.name: Schronisko PTTK Samotnia
accommodationStrategy.description: one night sleeping on the ridge shortens the Droga Przyjaźni day at both ends and lets you be on Śnieżka at sunrise. Bunk rooms, shared bathrooms, a warden's kitchen.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct with the hut by phone or its own form, 2–3 months ahead for summer weekends [VERIFY: current Samotnia bed rate].

accommodationStrategy.name: Willa Sanssouci
accommodationStrategy.description: parking on site (non-negotiable for the Stołowe days), a drying room, breakfast from 07:00, and fifteen minutes' drive to both Karłów and Błędne Skały.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead, direct by phone for the early breakfast.

logistics.connectivity: Play, Orange and T-Mobile all cover Karpacz, Kudowa and the ridge itself; the cirque floors and Kocioł Łomniczki are dead. On the crest your phone will hop onto Czech networks — Poland and Czechia are both EU, so roaming is free, but turn off data if you are near your fair-use cap.
logistics.emergency: **GOPR — 985 or 601 100 300**, or 112. Install the *Ratunek* app, which sends GPS coordinates automatically. Give your position by trail colour and the nearest schronisko.
logistics.weather: Śnieżka is one of the windiest inhabited places in Europe. Mean annual temperature at the observatory is about **0.4 °C**, mean wind speed roughly **12–13 m/s**, and it records gusts above 100 km/h on well over a hundred days a year, with recorded extremes near **290 km/h** [VERIFY: exact record gust and mean wind figures from IMGW]. Cloud sits on the summit around 300 days a year. There is no shelter on Równia pod Śnieżką. Carry a windshell always, even in July.
logistics.bookingWindows: Ridge huts (Samotnia, Strzecha Akademicka, Odrodzenie) 2–3 months for weekends. Szczeliniec and Błędne Skały use timed entry in high season — buy the day before. Jaskinia Niedźwiedzia needs a week or more in July–August.
logistics.money: Poland uses the złoty; roughly 4.3 PLN to the euro. Cards work almost everywhere including most schroniska, but carry 150–200 PLN in cash for hut kitchens, the Błędne Skały toll road and small bufety.
logistics.transportRules: The **ridge is an international border**. Both countries are in Schengen so crossing is trivial and unmarked, but **carry photo ID** — Czech and Polish police do occasionally check on the crest and at Pec pod Sněžkou. Marked trails only: leaving the trail in either national park is an offence, and the Karkonosze bogs are the reason.
logistics.permits: **Karkonoski PN** and **Park Narodowy Gór Stołowych** both charge daily entry, payable at gates, online or by QR code at trailheads [VERIFY: 2026 Góry Stołowe PN daily entry tariff]. Both ban wild camping, drones and dogs off-lead. Szczeliniec and Błędne Skały have fixed one-way circulation and their own additional tickets on top of park entry.

proTips: **Run the paved ridge sections in the dry, and never at speed in the wet.** Those granite setts are the single biggest injury cause in the Karkonosze; GOPR's ankle callouts cluster on them. If it rains, swap the Droga Przyjaśni day for the Skalne Grzyby.

**Shoes matter more than usual.** Take one pair with a stiff rock plate and hard lugs for the granite, and one softer, grippier pair for the sandstone. A single soft-lugged shoe will feel wrong on both ranges.
**Do Szczeliniec at 08:30 or at 17:00.** Between 10:00 and 15:00 in summer the slots become a stationary queue and the one-way system means you cannot escape forwards.
**The Czech side is the cheap lunch.** Soup and a beer at Pec pod Sněžkou or on the Czech ridge huts undercuts Karpacz noticeably, and it is a legitimate 30-minute detour from Równia pod Śnieżką.
**Buy the 7-day park ticket if you are running four or more days.** It costs a fraction of daily entries and the QR is checked by roving rangers on the ridge, not only at the gates.
**Ask for *"schronisko"*, not "hut".** And *"Czy tędy do Śnieżki?"* — "is this the way to Śnieżka?" — gets you an answer from anyone.
**Start the Droga Przyjaźni from Szrenica, not from Karpacz.** Running west-to-east puts the prevailing wind behind you and the Kopa chairlift at the finish rather than the start.

raw.Named routes, distance and vertical: (1) **Droga Przyjaźni Polsko-Czeskiej**, the red-blazed main ridge trail: Szrenica → Śnieżne Kotły → Wielki Szyszak → Równia pod Śnieżką → **Śnieżka (1,603 m)** → Przełęcz Okraj, roughly 28–30 km with about 900 m of cumulative climb once you are on the crest. (2) **Śnieżka loop from Karpacz** via Kocioł Łomniczki: 17 km, +1,050 m. (3) **Mały Staw / Wielki Staw tarn circuit**: 21 km, +900 m. (4) **Szczeliniec Wielki (919 m)** from Karłów: 6 km, +230 m, but slow. (5) **Błędne Skały + Skalne Grzyby link**: 22 km, +550 m. (6) **Śnieżnik (1,425 m)** from Kletno: 16 km, +900 m.
raw.Technical grade: The ridge is T1–T2 walking terrain that runs like T3 because of the surface. Kocioł Łomniczki and the Czarny Kocioł zigzags are T3. Szczeliniec's Piekiełko slots and Błędne Skały's passages are T2 by grade and unrunnable by geometry — you turn sideways and shuffle.
raw.Terrain: Four distinct surfaces: **stone-paved ridge trail** (irregular granite setts, laid to stop erosion, brutal underfoot and genuinely dangerous wet); **peat-bog boardwalk** across Równia pod Śnieżką (wet timber, zero grip, run it flat-footed); **granite tor and blockfield** in the cirque rims; and **sandstone slab and step** throughout the Stołowe, which is grippy dry and soapy wet.
raw.Water points by name: Karkonosze: **Schronisko Na Hali Szrenickiej**, **Schronisko Pod Łabskim Szczytem**, **Schronisko Odrodzenie** (Przełęcz Karkonoska), **Samotnia** and **Strzecha Akademicka** at Mały Staw, **Dom Śląski** at Równia pod Śnieżką (the last water before the summit cone), and the Poštovna post office hut on Śnieżka itself. Stołowe: **Schronisko PTTK na Szczelińcu Wielkim**, the bufet at Karłów, **Schronisko Pasterka**. There is nothing drinkable between Szrenica and Odrodzenie — carry 1.5 L.
raw.Bail-outs: From the ridge above Karpacz: the **Kolej linowa Kopa** chairlift (top station 1,375 m, a 25-minute descent from Śnieżka's saddle) runs you down to Karpacz in about 15 minutes [VERIFY: 2026 Kopa chairlift fare and operating hours]. From the western ridge: drop north to Szklarska Poręba on the blue or yellow trails, 40–60 minutes. From Równia pod Śnieżką you can also drop **south into Czechia** to Pec pod Sněžkou. In the Stołowe, every ridge point is within 5 km of the road 387 between Radków, Karłów and Kudowa.
